stories.title: The Train at Neeb Karori
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.location: Neeb Karori Railway Station, Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Maharaj-ji boarded a first-class compartment without a ticket. A conductor kicked him off in the rural stop of Neeb Karori. When the driver tried to start the train, the locomotive refused to move despite full steam pressure. Only after the station master and conductor begged Baba to reboard did the train move forward effortlessly.
stories.text: In the early days, Maharaj-ji boarded a first-class train compartment. At the rural village of Neeb Karori, an ticket collector discovered he had no ticket and rudely forced Baba off the train into the dusty heat. Baba sat quietly under a tree nearby, sticking his tongs (chimta) into the dirt. When the green flag waved, the driver opened the throttle, but the train would not budge an inch. They brought another locomotive to pull it, but that failed too. A local station master recognized Baba and warned the railway officials: 'You have insulted a great saint. Until he returns, this train will not move.' The ticket collector and conductor ran to Baba, apologized with folded hands, and begged him to return. Baba laughed playfully, agreed on two conditions: that the railway build a proper station for the poor villagers of Neeb Karori and that ticket collectors treat poor wanderers with kindness. When Baba stepped back on board, the train immediately surged forward without effort.
stories.teaching: Outer pride and authority crumble before pure spiritual innocence. Treat every wandering soul with kindness.

stories.title: Dr. Richard Alpert and His Mother's Spleen
stories.book: Be Here Now / Miracle of Love
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.summary: Harvard psychologist Dr. Richard Alpert sat before Maharaj-ji as a staunch Western skeptic. Baba looked into his eyes and asked why he had been thinking about his deceased mother and the spleen disease that killed her the previous night under the stars miles away. Alpert broke down in tears, dissolved his intellectual ego, and was reborn as Ram Dass.
stories.text: When Harvard psychologist Dr. Richard Alpert first traveled into the Himalayan foothills to meet Maharaj-ji, he was full of Western scientific skepticism. The previous night, sitting alone in the dark miles away in an apple orchard, Alpert had looked at the stars and thought tenderly of his mother, who had recently passed away in Boston from a disease of the spleen. He had told nobody about this intimate thought. The next morning, upon arriving at the ashram, Maharaj-ji looked right through him, smiled warmly, and asked in Hindi: 'You were thinking about your mother last night, weren't you? She died of spleen, yes?' Alpert felt as if an invisible laser had pierced through every defense mechanism of his psyche. In a single instant, his academic cynicism melted into uncontrollable weeping, experiencing unconditional love for the first time. He was rechristened 'Ram Dass' (Servant of God).
stories.teaching: The true guru knows every hidden chamber of your heart before you even utter a word, meeting you with boundless love.

stories.title: The Blanket of Bullets
stories.book: Miracle of Love / By His Grace
stories.author: Dada Mukerjee & Ram Dass
stories.summary: During WWII, a devotee's son was deployed on the battlefield. At night in India, Baba wrapped himself tightly in his heavy wool blanket, groaning in severe pain as if taking bullet hits. In the morning, Baba tossed the blanket down, and heavy lead bullets rolled onto the floor while Baba remained unscathed. A letter later arrived confirming the son had survived direct gunfire.
stories.text: During World War II, an Indian devotee couple had their only son serving on the dangerous frontlines overseas. One evening at Bhavania Ashram, Maharaj-ji suddenly lay down, pulled his heavy woolen blanket (kambal) completely over his head, and began groaning, tossing, and sweating through the night as if enduring intense mortar fire and agony. The devotees sat outside terrified, not daring to disturb him. At dawn, Baba threw the blanket aside and shook it out, heavy spent lead bullets cascaded onto the floor with a metallic clatter. Baba laughed and said, 'The boy was in great danger, but he is safe now.' Weeks later, a letter arrived from the front: the son wrote that his entire company had been ambushed and wiped out by machine-gun fire, but an invisible armor had shielded his chest, deflecting every bullet harmlessly away.
stories.teaching: A saint's grace is not bound by space or physical distance. Sincere devotion bridges thousands of miles instantly.

stories.title: Water Turned to Pure Ghee
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.summary: During a massive festival (bhandara) at Kainchi Dham, the cooks ran out of clarified butter (ghee) to fry puris for the waiting crowd. Baba instructed them to scoop buckets of cold water from the nearby river and pour it straight into the hot frying cauldrons. The water miraculously turned into pure, fragrant ghee.
stories.text: At a major festival in Kainchi Dham, thousands of pilgrims arrived unexpectedly from the surrounding mountain villages to receive darshan and prasad. The ashram kitchen was preparing mountains of puris, but halfway through the day, the cooks rushed to Maharaj-ji in distress: 'Baba, all the tins of ghee are empty! We have hundreds of hungry people waiting and no money or market open nearby.' Baba scolded them playfully: 'Why do you worry? Go take two large canisters down to the river, fill them with water, and pour it into the hot frying pans.' The cooks hesitated, fearing boiling oil and water would explode, but obeyed out of faith. When the river water touched the giant iron pans, it turned into sweet, fragrant golden ghee. The next morning, when new tins of ghee arrived from the market, Baba instructed: 'Now take two tins of ghee and pour them back into the river to repay Mother Ganga.'
stories.teaching: When service is done selflessly for God's children, the divine provides abundance out of thin air, but always honor nature with gratitude.

stories.title: Larry Brilliant and the WHO Smallpox Mission
stories.author: Dr. Larry Brilliant
stories.summary: Young American doctor Larry Brilliant wanted to meditate in the ashram in quiet contemplation. Baba poked him and ordered him to go work for the United Nations World Health Organization to eradicate smallpox. Despite having no contacts, Larry was hired, and smallpox was successfully wiped out from India.
stories.text: Dr. Larry Brilliant had left his medical career in America to seek enlightenment, sitting peacefully under the trees of Kainchi Dham in white robes. One afternoon, Maharaj-ji summoned him, tapped him firmly on the ribs, and said loudly: 'Doctor, why are you wasting your time sitting here with your eyes closed? Go to New Delhi and work for the World Health Organization. You are going to eradicate smallpox from India! This is God's gift to suffering humanity.' Larry was bewildered; he had no money, no connections at the UN, and smallpox had plagued humanity for three thousand years. He went to Delhi and was rejected repeatedly, but kept returning because Baba insisted. Eventually, an opening appeared; Larry joined the WHO team as a key leader, and within a few years, India celebrated its very last case of smallpox. Millions of lives were spared.
stories.teaching: True spirituality is not escaping the world into passive trance; it is dedicating your skills to the practical alleviation of human suffering.

stories.title: Never Throw Banana Peels
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.summary: When a devotee casually tossed a banana peel onto the ground, Baba immediately stopped him and reminded everyone that nothing in God's creation is waste, for all of life is divine and interconnected.
stories.text: A devotee was eating a banana near Maharaj-ji's wooden takhat and casually threw the skin onto the path. Maharaj-ji immediately leaned forward with a look of genuine concern: 'Why did you throw that away like that? Pick it up! Even a cow, a bird, or an ant can take nourishment from it. Nothing in God's creation is waste. See God in everything, even a banana peel.' The devotee gathered the peel and placed it respectfully near a feeding trough where a wandering cow ate it moments later. Baba used everyday simplicity to teach profound non-dual Vedanta: that there is no 'sacred' separate from 'ordinary', everything belongs to the Divine.
stories.teaching: Respect every scrap of creation. When you live with conscious reverence, no resource is wasted and no living creature is neglected.

stories.title: Feeding the Abusive Man with Sweets
stories.author: Dada Mukerjee
stories.summary: A man filled with bitter hatred arrived at the house where Baba was staying, shouting insults and accusations. Instead of showing anger, Baba welcomed him with open arms, fed him rich sweets, and treated him like a long-lost son. The man broke into tears and prostrated in repentance.
stories.text: In Allahabad, a local man had become fiercely jealous of Maharaj-ji's growing reputation and arrived outside the house shouting angry slanders and harsh abuses. The devotees rushed to shut the gate and call for help, but Maharaj-ji stopped them instantly: 'Do not touch him! Bring him inside immediately.' When the red-faced man was ushered into the room, Baba stood up, wrapped him in a blanket, and shouted to the kitchen: 'Quickly! Bring hot puris, kachoris, and jalebis! My son has come from so far and he is exhausted and hungry!' Baba fed the man with his own hands, patting his back with tender affection. Disarmed by pure warmth where he expected retaliation, the man collapsed at Baba's feet, weeping bitterly: 'Baba, I came to curse you, and you feed me like a mother.' Baba stroked his head: 'Everyone is suffering, beta. Anger is only pain shouting for love.'
stories.teaching: Never fight hatred with anger. Love and nourishment disarm the darkest hostility.

stories.title: The Mysterious Car with an Empty Tank
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.summary: A devotee was driving Maharaj-ji late at night through a deserted mountain road when the petrol gauge dropped to dead empty with miles to go. Baba patted the dashboard and commanded the driver to keep driving. The car drove for hours over mountain passes until reaching safety.
stories.text: Late one evening, a devotee named Mr. Tewari was chauffeuring Maharaj-ji through a desolate mountain stretch between Bareilly and Almora. Suddenly, the engine spluttered and the fuel gauge pointer dropped below empty. There was not a petrol station for thirty miles, and the road was pitch dark and freezing cold. The driver panicked: 'Maharaj-ji, the petrol is finished! We are stranded on this mountain pass.' Baba hit the dashboard with his hand and laughed heartily: 'Drive, you foolish man! Don't look at the dial, look at the road!' The driver stepped on the accelerator, and the car hummed smoothly. They drove for nearly forty-five miles across steep mountain climbs. When they finally rolled into a town station the next morning, the mechanic removed the fuel cap and tapped the tank: it was bone-dry. The car had traveled on faith and Baba's word alone.
stories.teaching: When you surrender anxiety and focus purely on your duty, divine grace carries you far past human limitation.

stories.title: Planting Seeds in Every Soul
stories.author: Ram Dass
stories.summary: Ram Dass once questioned Baba for praising and giving blessings to worldly, hypocritical visitors. Baba explained that by telling someone they are a great devotee, he plants a divine seed in their heart that will eventually blossom.
stories.text: One afternoon at Vrindavan, a prominent politician known for dishonesty and corruption visited the ashram. To Ram Dass's dismay, Maharaj-ji greeted the politician warmly, praised him, and placed a garland around his neck, calling him a 'great devotee of Lord Ram.' Later, when the visitor departed, Ram Dass expressed his confusion: 'Maharaj-ji, that man is known to be corrupt! Why did you tell him he is a great bhakta?' Baba looked at Ram Dass with profound gentleness: 'Ram Dass, if I tell a man he is bad, he will become worse. But if I tell him he is a devotee of God, I have planted a sacred seed in his consciousness. Day and night, he will wonder: Can I become worthy of what Baba saw in me? If even ten out of a hundred people change their life from that seed, the world becomes a better place.'
stories.teaching: Always address the highest divinity in others, never their lowest flaws. Seeing the good in people inspires them to rise toward it.

stories.title: Taking on the Devotee's Illness
stories.author: Dada Mukerjee
stories.summary: When a devotee fell critically ill with high fever, Baba would often begin shivering and running a high temperature himself. As Baba's fever broke, the devotee's illness vanished, demonstrating the saint taking on the karma of his disciples.
stories.text: Dada Mukerjee recorded numerous instances where devotees on the brink of death or suffering from agonizing illnesses suddenly recovered after Baba visited them. In Allahabad, an elderly devotee was afflicted with virulent pneumonia; doctors had given up hope. That night, Baba retired to his room, groaning and clutching his chest, coughing violently while his body burned with high fever. His disciples watched helplessly as Baba suffered through the night. By morning, Baba took a bath, drank tea, and was completely healthy. At the same time, the doctor visited the sick devotee and was stunned to find his lungs completely clear and fever gone. When devotees asked Baba about it, he waved his hand dismissively: 'Doctors know nothing. Ram takes care of everything.'
stories.teaching: The true satguru silently absorbs the suffering of those who call on him with sincere faith.

stories.title: The Incarnation of Hanuman (Hanuman Ansh Babaji)
stories.author: Ravi Prakash Pande & Ram Dass
stories.summary: Maharaj-ji was born as Lakshmi Narayan Sharma around 1900 in Akbarpur village, Firozabad district, Uttar Pradesh. Revered across the world as Hanuman Ansh (the divine incarnation of Lord Hanuman), he lived in complete humility, constantly repeating the name of Ram and establishing sacred Hanuman temples at Hanumangadh, Kainchi Dham, Vrindavan, and Lucknow.
stories.text: Maharaj-ji was born around 1900 into a pious Brahmin family in the village of Akbarpur, Firozabad district, Uttar Pradesh, and was named Lakshmi Narayan Sharma. From his earliest years, his heart was consumed by divine longing. Leaving home in his teens, he wandered Northern India as an ascetic under names such as Lakshman Das, Handi Wale Baba, and Tikonia Wale Baba, practicing intense sadhana. In the village of Neeb Karori, through a famous train lila, he became known as Baba Neem Karoli. Throughout his life, devotees and saints recognized him as Hanuman Ansh, a direct incarnation and living presence of Lord Hanuman. Though he possessed boundless supernatural powers, he remained utterly humble, wrapped in a simple plaid blanket, deflecting all praise back to Lord Hanuman and Ram. He established Hanumangadh in Nainital in 1950, founded the world-renowned Kainchi Dham ashram in 1964, and built numerous Hanuman temples before taking Mahasamadhi in Vrindavan on September 11, 1973.
stories.teaching: True greatness lies in absolute humility and single-minded remembrance of the Divine, serving all without seeking personal praise.

stories.text: [Ashrams & Sacred Places: Kainchi | Source: maharajji.love] After the Kainchi ashram was built, Babaji began spending the summer months there. In 1964, when some devotees were going there, I was asked to accompany them. I explained that I had to stay back because Babaji might visit at any time. When the devotees got to Kainchi, Baba asked what my reply had been when invited to come to Kainchi. Then Babaji said, "Dada cannot leave his house because of my unscheduled visits. But those who are near to me do not bother about me." In May 1966, we received a letter from Babaji, who was already in Kainchi, asking us to come as soon as the university closed. Didi and I reached there within a week. This was our first visit. Babaji was waiting for us in his room. While sitting with him, a devotee brought a basket of various kinds of fruits from his garden. Babaji took out some of the fruits and showed me which I might eat and which I should avoid. After I had my tea and prasad , he took me around the ashram. It took only a few days to get acquainted with the routine going on in the ashram. This little temple is hidden beneath a flyover of Mahatma Gandhi Marg near the Yamuna River in North New Delhi. Inaugurated on December 4, 1965, this temple is now almost 'secret'. It is very difficult to find with a very obscure entrance in an unlikely place just north of the Ladakh Tibetan Market. This temple along with the small ashram was built by Maharajji and funded by Jugal Kishor Birla, who had no children and left his fortune to various religious trusts. Before the temple was built, Maharajji said that there was an old Hanumanji murti (statue) buried in the ground at the spot where this Hanumanji temple is located. The murti was dug up and now sits in front of Hanumanji within the temple. For many years the pujari and 'caretaker' of this temple was named Sri Narayan Swami. The temple is operated by his family, under the Hanuman Ashram Society, one of J.K. Birla's religious trusts. Each morning Swamiji used to complete arati at this temple and travel by auto rickshaw to Maharajji's South Delhi Ashram for arati and pujari seva, a distance of some 35 kilometers (22 miles). In the evening, Swamiji returned to Baba's North Delhi Ashram by auto rickshaw for evening arati. Narayan Swami left his body on August 8, 2020. His sons continue taking care of the temple. This temple is very deserving of contributions to be directed toward maintenance, plastering, painting, and upkeep. Sundarkand on Tuesday evenings Inaugurated in 1951, this is reportedly the first temple established by Maharajji. This extensive ridge top temple has exquisite views on a clear day. Hanumanghari temple is about 2 km from Nanital. It's a nice walk if the skies are clear. If it's raining you can go by car. Arati is performed daily, morning and evening. It is located on Rishikesh Haridwar road at a place named Veerbhadra, at a distance of 6 km from Rishikesh. This piece of land remained vacant under the care of a certain man for many years. Babaji left his physical body in 1973. He had always done lila in his bodily form, but his psychic resolves are being made good even now. Shri Siddhi Ma caused a stir by raising the issue about this place in 1984. Consequently the land was legally occupied and his devotees got built a magnificent Hanuman temple. A grand bhandara is held here every year on Hanuman Jayanti (Chaitra-Poonima). In the beginning Hanuman temple was small and Babaji was not satisfied with it. Hence, a huge and magnificent temple was erected for Hanumanji within three or four years. It was inaugurated on Shri Hanuman Jayanti 1993 with grand celebrations and a large gathering had prasad in bhandara as always. Long ago Babaji had told Shri Siddhi Ma that he would set up a 27 ft. high Hanuman murti at this place in Rishikesh so that the passers-by may have his darshan from outside. Hanumanji (in the mind of Maharajji) was so much delighted with the beauty of that place that he liked to stay there. Therefore, in the sixth decade, the then Lt. By Babaji's grace this Hanuman temple at Shimla has gained so much recognition that various celebrations are organized every now and then and not only the devotees but the tourists also enthusiastically participate in them. Especially on Ramnavmi, the foundation day of the temple, thousands of devotees have prasad in bhandara. Now the bhandara is held on every Sunday. It appeared that the work was incomplete without the temple of Babaji Maharaj. So, by the inspiration of Shri Siddhi Ma, the trustees of the temple decided to build Babaji Maharaj's temple and to install his Murti therein. Shri Veerbhadra Singh, the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh laid the foundation stone on 10 April 1995. The temple was completed and inaugurated on Ramnavmi, 25 March 1999, with grand celebrations. In 1942, Poornanand Tewari had gone to Nainital to get some papers connected with his law- suit. As he missed the bus, he was coming back to Kainchi on foot via Gathia. It was the dark of night and the tired and frightened Tewari was passing by Khufia danth, so-called a haunted place. He saw a bulky man wrapped in a blanket by the Khufia danth. He was scared but that man called him by name telling him the reason of his (Tewari's) coming there at that odd hour. He was none else but Baba Neeb Karoliji Maharaj. Tewari felt somewhat comfortable. Babaji talked to him for a little while and asked him to go forward fearlessly and that he would get a public transport ahead. While staying there Sri Ma had the desire to visit Baba's birthplace, the village of Akbarpur. It was a sudden decision to go in such cold winter days. She and the devotees left for Hirangau by train on 17 January, and from there they went to the village. Sri Ma was not known to anyone in Akbarpur, and since no prior information was sent, no one was there to receive her. There was no appropriate place to stay in the village, and in the prevailing circumstances, it was very difficult for them to make their own arrangements. Nevertheless, Baba had said that all that is auspicious would be with Sri Ma, and in keeping with his words, his grace began to flow and provide for her. Shri Ram Sanehi came to know of Sri Ma's arrival and extended hospitality to her and the accompanying devotees. An old man who had come with Sri Ma happened to ask Ram Sanehi, "Do you ever see Baba in your dream?" Nodding in affirmation, Ram Sanehi said, "Sometimes." "When did you see him last?" Ram Sanehi replied with a smile, "Last night." He hesitated to reply, but when pressed he said, "Laxmi Narain [Baba's name in Akbarpur] said, 'Sri Ma is coming. Extend all hospitality. Don't let us down.'" After tea Ram Sanehi took everyone to Dak Bangalia, the place where Baba used to live, since Sri Ma wanted to stay there. The house had remained closed for the last fifteen years, and Shyam Sunder, a teacher of young offenders at Itawa Jail, kept the keys. Since he was on duty, Ram Sanehi was helpless, but Baba's lila came into play again. But I did see him, and since it was one of the most memorable events of my life, I want to add my voice to those who speak of his greatness. (If you do not know about his life, please read some of the books about him. They are a great inspiration.) I was in Brindaban with some of the members of our ashram for the Samyam Sapta with Anandamayi Ma. After a few days quite a number of Americans and Europeans began showing up for Ma’s darshan, which was a sign that Neem Karoli Baba must be in town. We knew where his ashram was, so one morning we went to see him. And that was all we did: see. I have no idea why, but for decades the police in that area had been paranoid about American and European tourists and really made a nuisance of themselves. A few months before my first trip to India one of my close friends went to travel with Ma Anandamayi, and every single day she was in Brindaban officious fools came and pestered her, acting as though she was a spy or mad bomber. Over the years I heard about these antics, though I never experienced any myself. But they apparently had decided after so many years that Anandamayi Ma’s devotees were not spies and had shifted their suspicion to the devotees of Neem Karoli Baba. As a consequence when we got to the ashram we found the gate was locked. stories.text: [Ashrams & Sacred Places: Temples Are for Everyone | Source: maharajji.love] Maharajji was here to help the downtrodden. “Once Babaji went to Hanuman temple, Lucknow by Kehar Singh's car. Umadatta Shukla also was with them. Babaji went into the temple and facing Hanumanji sat by the fence on the road-side. The driver also desired to have Hanumanji's darshan. Therefore, he locked the car and went into the temple by the bridge at the side of the road. When Shuklaji saw him he came running and met him half-way on the bridge and jostled him out. The Supreme Being' Babaji, though He had His back towards them saw all this. He came running and set the driver free with such force that Umadatta could not bear the push and fell on one side. Admonishing Shuklaji He asked, ‘Who are you to stop him? Do you think I have built this temple for you? It has been built for them (low castes, poor, miserable and afflicted).’ Saying so He took that Koiri (a low caste), holding him by the hand, to Hanumanji and bending His head made him to pranaam Hanumanji. Kehar Singhji was an eye-witness to this incident.” (Endnote: from "Prem Avatar") EVERYONE gets jaoed (sent away) at some point. And that's okay. Gurudatji told how “Maharajji jaoed many people. VIPs would come and get their ladhus (a sweet) and they would want to remain with Maharajji. But Maharajji would snap His fingers and point for them to go. stories.text: [Ashrams & Sacred Places: How We Do Aarti - Vrindavan - 5 Videos | Source: maharajji.love] Aarti is practiced every day, morning and evening, at all the temples in Maharajji's ashrams. This is the Aarti practice done at the Mahasamdhi Temple of India's great saint Neeb Karoli Baba / Neem Karoli Baba Maharajji in Vrindavan, India on the morning of Hanuman Jayanti in 1999. Aarti is said to have descended from the Vedic concept of fire rituals, or homa . In the traditional aarti ceremony, the flower represents the earth (solidity), the water and accompanying handkerchief correspond with the water element (liquidity), the lamp or candle represents the fire component (heat), the peacock fan conveys the precious quality of air (movement), and the yak-tail fan represents the subtle form of ether (space). The incense represents a purified state of mind, and one’s "intelligence" is offered through the adherence to rules of timing and order of offerings. Thus, one’s entire existence and all facets of material creation are symbolically offered to the Lord via the aarti ceremony. (Wikipedia) Aarti is offered to Maharajji with the Utmost Love and Gratitude. In Part 1, you will hear the bell aarti. This aarti begins at Maharajji's mahasamadhi mandir, moves to Maharajji's Kutir, then moves to Shivaji temple, then salutes Tulsi plant and returns to Maharajji's temple. stories.summary: [Ashrams & Sacred Places: Heaven at Shri Vrindavandham | Source: maharajji.love] Those who had the darshan of Baba Neem Karoli, the wandering yogi, never knew that he would create a heaven for them at Shri Vrindavandham, a sacred pilgrimage center. H...
stories.text: [Ashrams & Sacred Places: Heaven at Shri Vrindavandham | Source: maharajji.love] Those who had the darshan of Baba Neem Karoli, the wandering yogi, never knew that he would create a heaven for them at Shri Vrindavandham, a sacred pilgrimage center. He had already prepared a back- ground for it when Shri Ma had the first darshan of him in 1944. Asking her to come near him 'he then told her "I will build a hut for you in Vrindavan" Shri Ma did not grasp the meaning then, nor did she pay any attention to it. The truth of the Master's utterance had to come out. In due course of time, not only the huts for Shri Ma and Maharaj, but Baba Neeb Karoli ashram and Hanuman temple and that of 'Vrindeshwari' (the goddess of Vrindavan) were built in a vast area of land. A commemorative temple has also been built over the mortal remains of Babaji Maharaj. Babaji transformed the uneven land, full of thorny leafless shrubs and gokharu (a thorny medicinal plant) located on the 'parikrama marg' (circular road to go round Vrindavan), into good, even land by putting his sacred feet. He very often went there and sat on the platform of Hathiwale Baba's hut and ruminated over his plan. Leaving behind his attendants in different hospices in Vrindavan town, he occupied himself converting that rough and rugged land on 'parikrama marg' into an ashram. When Shri Ma saw that piece of land she asked, 'where have you taken this piece of land? And who will come to this lonely, rough and rugged place to have darshan?" Maharajji replied, "you will see, it will be inhabited and will develop into a township one day." How his words proved to be true, it may be ascertained by visiting the place now. Following Hanuman Chalisa and kirtan both evenings end with aarti at 8:30 pm. Throughout the year we honor different aspects of the Divine and celebrate festivals from Hindu, Christian and Buddhist traditions. All festivals take place at Sri Neem Karoli Baba Mandir . This ashram, dedicated to Sri Neem Karoli Baba, is located in Southern Germany in Ulm - halfway between the cities of Munich and Stuttgart. It was founded by Sri Durgamayi Ma in 1998 and serves as refuge of spiritual practice for Maharajji’s Satsang in Germany, which has grown over the years. In 1971 Durgamayi Ma saw a picture of Sri Neem Karoli Baba in the book ‘Be Here Now’ by Ram Dass. Feeling a very strong longing, she and her spiritual companion Vishnu Digambar travelled to India, were found by Maharajji and became His devotees. Meeting Baba changed the course of their lives. teachings.quote: Love everyone. You can't be angry when you see God in them.
teachings.guidance: Love is not an emotional transaction or something you bargain for. When you love without conditions, you reflect the nature of your own soul. See the light of God inside the person who irritates you, and resentment evaporates.

teachings.quote: Serve everyone. The best way to find God is to feed the hungry.
teachings.guidance: Do not wait until you are wealthy to serve. Give your time, give a smile, offer comfort to the lonely. When you feed someone with your own hands, you are feeding the Lord residing in their belly.

teachings.quote: What can fear give you? Nothing. What can faith give you? Everything.
teachings.guidance: Anxiety is the mind trying to manipulate outcomes that belong to God. Perform your daily duties with sincerity and dedication, and surrender the final outcome to the Divine. You are never walking alone.

teachings.quote: Forgive others, not for their sake, but for your own peace.
teachings.guidance: Holding onto grudges is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to suffer. Forgive quietly, hold no malice in your thoughts, and keep your heart unburdened.

teachings.quote: Keep Ram's name on your lips always. It is your shield against all fear.
teachings.guidance: Chant while walking, while working, while eating. Slowly, the holy vibration purifies the mental atmosphere and anchors the wandering mind in divine stillness.
